Khalid vs The State Of Bihar on 17 July, 2025 Author: Chandra Shekhar Jha Bench: Chandra Shekhar Jha In The High Court Of Judicature At Patna Criminal Miscellaneous No.54154 of 2023 Arising Out of Ps. Case No.-10 Year-2014 Thana- Begusarai Complaint Case District- Begusarai ====================================================== 1. Md. Khalid Kabir @ Md. Khalid, Son of Late Kabir Uddin 2. Abul Hasnat @ Hasannat, Son of Abul Barkat, 3. Taran @ Md. Saleh, Son of Md. Kashim 4. Taw @ Taj Haidar Son of Obaidur Rahman 5. Shah Fahim Ahmad @ Shabab, Son of Sayad Shah Shamim Ahmad All are resident of Village-Lakhminiya Pachim Tola, Ward No. 16, P.S.- Balia, Dist- Begusarai ... ... Petitioners Versus 1. The State of Bihar 2. Samsadujjama, Son of Late Md. Idrish, Resident of Village-Lakhminiya P.S.- Balia, Dist- Begusarai ... ... Opposite Parties ===================================================== = Appearance : For the Petitioners : Mr. Bindhyachal Singh, Senior Advocate Mr. Vipin Kumar Singh, Advocate Ms. Nikita Mittal, Advocate Mr. Kumar Awnish Ankit, Advocate For the State : Md. Fahimuddin, App For the O.P. No.2 : Mr. Ansul, Senior Advocate Mr. Mrityunjay Kumar, Advocate
texts.facts: The present application has been preferred under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure (in short 'CrPC') on behalf of the petitioners for quashing of the order dated 06.08.2022 passed by the learned Judicial Magistrate, Railway, Barauni in connection with Complaint Case No.10 of 2014, where the learned jurisdictional Magistrate took cognizance against the petitioners for the offences punishable under Sections 147, 341, 323, 379 and 302 of the Indian Penal Code (in short 'CrPC'). 3. First Information Report (in short 'FIR') speaks in brief about the case of prosecution based upon information supplied by the informant/complainant, namely, Samsadujjama, son of Late Md. Idrish, resident of village- Lakhminiya, P.S.- Balia, Distt.- Begusarai that on14.04.2014 at 10.00 hours, while he was going to Begusarai for eye check up along with his son Nazisu Zama (deceased), Naseer Zama and wife Kashma Khatoon, when they boarded the train at Lakminyan Railway Station, all the above-named petitioners along with 2-3 unknown persons, who are also resident of Lakminyan, P.S.-Baliya, District-Begusarai snatched the Patna High Court CR. MISC. No.54154 of 2023 dt.17-07-2025 3/20 purse of his wife. When his son Nazisu Zama made an attempt to catch the snatcher, all the above-named Md. Khalid Kabir @ Md. Khalid vs The State Of Bihar on 17 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/94929467/ 2 petitioners pushed him from train, out of which, his son suffered severe injuries. The informant somehow managed to get the train stopped and picked up his injured son and brought him to Dr. S. Pandit at Begusarai for treatment, who referred him to another hospital from where, his injured son was brought to Dr. Nalini Ranjan, who also referred his injured son to Sadar Hospital, Begusarai, where he succumbed to injuries. 4. With the aforesaid information, initially Begusarai Rail P.S. Case No.06 of 2014 was lodged. After investigation, the accused/petitioners were exonerated from the allegation, and final form bearing No.22 of 2014 dated 31.08.2014 was submitted by the police. The aforesaid final form was accepted by the learned Railway Magistrate also. 5. The informant preferred a protest petition no.10 C of 2015 on 17.05.2014 after a lapse of one month of occurrence, where, considering the statement of the complainant and enquiry witnesses on oath, the learned Patna High Court CR. MISC. No.54154 of 2023 dt.17-07-2025 Jurisdictional Magistrate took cognizance for the offences punishable under Sections 147, 341, 323, 379 and 302 of the IPC against the petitioners. It is an admitted position that for the Patna High Court CR. MISC. No.54154 of 2023 dt.17-07-2025 occurrence, initially, the FIR was lodged by the complainant, which was registered as Begusarai Rail P.S. Case No.06 of 2014, which, after thorough investigation by the police, exonerated the accused/petitioners and, thereafter, the final form was submitted on 31.08.2014 by the police. It also appears that treating protest as complaint case, cognizance was taken against petitioners. It would be apposite to reproduce the impugned cognizance order dated 06.08.2022, which is as under:- "IN THE COURT OF J.M. RAILWAY, BARAUNI Complaint case no.10 of 2014 06-08-2022 Today record is put for cognizance cum summoning order. Attendance of complainant is filed. This is complaint case filed by Shamshaduzzaman against Md. Khalid, Hasannat, Shabab, Taran and Taw. The case of the complainant in brief is that on dated 14.04.2014 at 10:00 AM he along with his family, sons Najusu Janna, Nasir Janna and wife Kashama Khatoon took train from Lakhaminia Station to going at Begusarai. When train was just start to ran all accused persons along with 2-3 unknown persons came to his compartment and one Md. Khalid snatched his wife's purse, his son Najisu Janna tried to protect they push him out from train. Due to which later on his son died. The offence committed due to old enemity. In support of her case complainant produced two enquiry witnesses namely, (I) Nasin Hussain, (ii) Kashma Khatoon.
texts.arguments: 6. It is submitted by Mr. Bindhyachal Singh, learned senior counsel appearing for petitioners that almost the same allegation/statement was made by the informant, who is the complainant and also by inquiry witnesses, who recorded their statement under Section 161 of CrPC during the course of investigation also. It is submitted that the postmortem report of the deceased categorically stated that he died out of accident. It is submitted that the petitioners and informant/complainant were known to each other, having previous enmity, and when the son of the informant/complainant died in a rail accident, out of a malicious approach to settle the score qua previous enmity, the present false case was lodged. It is submitted that the protest petition was filed after a lapse of one month from the date of lodging of the FIR in a premeditated and well- conceived manner. It is submitted by Mr. Singh that the complainant categorically stated on court question that he Patna High Court CR. MISC. No.54154 of 2023 dt.17-07-2025 never saw the postmortem report. He also admitted to the inimical term with petitioners/accused persons due to the "Mukhiya" election. It is submitted by Mr. Singh that the postmortem report was available on record, which categorically suggest that the Md. Khalid Kabir @ Md. Khalid vs The State Of Bihar on 17 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/94929467/ 3 injury received by the deceased son of the informant was due to a train accident, but this document of unimpeaching nature was completely ignored by learned Magistrate before taking cognizance against the petitioners. 7. Mr. Singh further pointed out that the statement of Enquiry Witness No.1, namely, Naseer Hussain and Enquiry Witness No.2, namely, Kashma Khatoon were completely ignored before taking cognizance in such a heinous matter, particularly, when police authority after in depth investigation, exonerated the petitioners from the allegation. 8. In support of his submission, Mr. Singh relied upon the court question of EW-1 and EW-2, where they categorically stated that the deceased fell from the train. It is pointed out that the postmortem report was obtained by EW- 1 (son of the complainant), but this fact was completely Patna High Court CR. MISC. No.54154 of 2023 dt.17-07-2025 ignored by the complainant and the same was not brought on record intentionally, and if it was so, perhaps the cognizance would not had been taken against the petitioners for the alleged offences. 9. In view of the aforesaid factual submissions, while concluding the argument, it is submitted by Mr. Singh that the implication of the petitioners is, admittedly, a consequence of village level political rivalry stemming from the election of the Mukhiya. It is further submitted that the informant/complainant, taking undue advantage of the accidental death of his son, has falsely implicated the petitioners in grave offences, including that of murder, despite their innocence. We may, however, note that in Hamdard Dawakhana (Wakf) v. Union of India [AIR 1965 SC 1167 : (1965) 2 SCR 192] an Patna High Court CR. MISC. No.54154 of 2023 dt.17-07-2025 argument was raised that the Md. Khalid Kabir @ Md. Khalid vs The State Of Bihar on 17 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/94929467/ 8 18. It would also be apposite to reproduce para- Patna High Court CR. MISC. No.54154 of 2023 dt.17-07-2025 102 of the legal report of the Hon'ble Supreme Court as available through Bhajan Lal's case (supra), which is as under:- "102. (2) Where the allegations in the first information report and other materials, if any, accompanying the FIR do not disclose a cognizable offence, justifying Patna High Court CR. MISC. No.54154 of 2023 dt.17-07-2025 an investigation by police officers under Section 156(1) of the Code except under an order of a Magistrate within the Md. Khalid Kabir @ Md. Khalid vs The State Of Bihar on 17 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/94929467/ 9 purview of Section 155(2) of the Code. (3) Where the uncontroverted allegations made in the FIR or complaint and the evidence collected in support of the same do not disclose the commission of any offence and make out a case against the accused. (6) Where there is an express legal bar engrafted in any of the provisions of the Code or the Act concerned (under which a criminal proceeding is instituted) to the institution and Patna High Court CR. MISC. No.54154 of 2023 dt.17-07-2025 continuance of the proceedings and/or where there is a specific provision in the Code or the Act concerned, providing efficacious redress for the grievance of the aggrieved party. (7) Where a criminal proceeding is manifestly attended with mala fide and/or where the proceeding is maliciously instituted with an ulterior motive for wreaking vengeance on the accused and with a view to spite him due to private and personal grudge."
